recipes.title: Build an open-source FPGA toolchain
recipes.description: Choose a flow by target-device support, HDL dialect, implementation stage and required verification. This guide separates synthesis, place-and-route, formal checking and waveform inspection; a toolchain bundle does not make every device backend production-ready.

picks.label: Start with a bundled toolchain
picks.reason: Provides coordinated binaries for synthesis, formal verification, place-and-route, programming and testing across Windows, macOS and Linux.
picks.tradeoff: Component versions and supported FPGA architectures vary; confirm your board and exact backend before relying on it.

picks.label: Scriptable RTL synthesis
picks.reason: Permissively licensed synthesis framework with Verilog support and a synthesizable SystemVerilog subset.
picks.tradeoff: Does not alone provide a complete FPGA implementation flow or universal device support.

picks.label: Open-source implementation
picks.reason: Timing-driven place-and-route for several Lattice, Gowin and other documented architectures.
picks.tradeoff: Architecture databases and bitstream tools are separate; some backends remain experimental.

picks.label: Add formal property checking
picks.reason: Adds solver-backed formal verification to supported Yosys designs.
picks.tradeoff: Results depend on correct assumptions, properties and solver configuration; it is not a simulator.

recipes.title: Choose an HDL simulator and debugger
recipes.description: Start with the design language and simulator semantics, then choose a testbench framework and waveform viewer. A verification framework is not a simulator, and a waveform viewer does not execute a design.

picks.label: VHDL simulation
picks.reason: Analyzes, compiles and simulates VHDL with native-code backends on Windows, macOS and Linux.
picks.tradeoff: VHDL-2008/2019 support is partial; synthesis integration is experimental.

picks.label: Event-driven Verilog simulation
picks.reason: Provides a simple compiler-plus-VVP runtime for supported Verilog and a growing SystemVerilog subset.
picks.tradeoff: SystemVerilog support is incomplete; it is not a full vendor simulator.

picks.label: Compiled SystemVerilog and lint
picks.reason: Generates C++/SystemC models and supports lint, coverage and compiled simulation workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Requires a C++/SystemC harness and is not a traditional event-driven simulator.

picks.label: Python testbenches
picks.reason: Lets teams write reusable Python testbenches against supported simulators.
picks.tradeoff: A compatible simulator and interface are still required; simulator-specific limitations apply.

picks.label: Inspect waveform traces
picks.reason: Views common VCD, FST and GHW trace files from HDL simulation runs.
picks.tradeoff: It only inspects traces and does not simulate or verify the design.
